title: From Alcohol Dependence to Financial Stability
subtitle:
A Journey of Recovery and Self-Reliance Through IRCA in Karnataka
Counselling, Therapeutic Interventions and Family Support Help 33-Year-Old Ramesh Gowda from Kolar Rebuild His Life
Ministry-Supported De-addiction Centre Helps Beneficiary Restore Family Relationships and Revive Business Activities
body_text: The journey of 33 year Ramesh Gowda (name changed) from alcohol dependence and financial difficulties towards improved well-being, stronger family relationships and renewed livelihood opportunities, offers an encouraging example of recovery supported by individual determination, professional counselling and family involvement. Mr. Ramesh Gowda, a resident of Kolar district in Karnataka, has made significant progress towards recovery from alcohol dependence through counselling and rehabilitation assistance at the Alcohol and Drug Abuse Free De-addiction Centre, an Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA). His experience highlights the importance of timely professional support and family encouragement in rebuilding personal and professional life. Belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) community, Ramesh previously ran his own business. What began as occasional alcohol consumption gradually became regular amid family-related difficulties and stress. His growing dependence affected the management of his business, weakened financial stability and strained relationships with family members. Recognising these challenges and determined to improve his circumstances, he voluntarily approached the IRCA centre in Kolar for assistance. He received support beginning on January 6, 2024, including regular counselling, motivational guidance and therapeutic interventions designed to help him understand his personal goals and responsibilities. The counselling process helped Ramesh reflect on the effects of alcohol dependence, strengthen his motivation and build confidence in pursuing recovery. The centre also conducted family counselling sessions to improve communication and understanding among family members and encourage a supportive environment for rehabilitation. With sustained guidance and family support, Ramesh showed significant improvement in his behaviour and overall well-being. As his confidence returned, he was able to regain focus on his business activities and work towards greater financial stability. The progress was also reflected in his family relationships. Improved communication and renewed attention to his responsibilities helped him rebuild healthier connections with his loved ones and pursue a more stable daily routine. Following counselling and rehabilitation support, Ramesh has regained stability in his personal and professional life and is now earning approximately ₹15,000 per month. This reported income reflects his renewed engagement with livelihood activities; the information provided does not specify his earlier monthly earnings. The Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts in Kolar demonstrates the value of accessible counselling, therapeutic interventions and family-based support for individuals affected by substance dependence. Such assistance can help beneficiaries strengthen their well-being and participate more confidently in family and economic life. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment supports rehabilitation and drug demand reduction interventions under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), including assistance through Integrated Rehabilitation Centres for Addicts.
